programme.title: Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live "Crushing It"
programme.desc: The Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live team loves the exhilarating jumps and stunts during a show, but nothing beats the excitement we bring to those most important to us, the fans. Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live hits the road as Demo Derby visits kids at Victory Junction, a camp for children with serious or chronic medical conditions.

programme.title: XOR - Xtreme Off-Road
programme.desc: Jeremy and Eliza finish up mounting the adjustable shocks add the Raptor-like fiberglass skin to the Prerunner Ranger.
programme.sub-title: Prerunner Ranger Suspension Mods and Fiberglass Panels

programme.title: Carcass
programme.desc: We bring our C1500 Abandoned Chevy back into the shop for an easy to install EFI setup that will allow for more boost and power. Plus we head out to Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course to compete with our Spec Panther race car.
programme.sub-title: Adding An EFI Setup To The C1500 Chevy

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: We work on the Triple Threat Camaro... and play at the OSCR drag race in Bowling Green, KY.

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Tommy and Joel roll an '83 Hurst Olds into the shop and install brakes, wheels, and tires to lay the groundwork for adding some thunder back into this classic lightning shifted street seeker.
programme.sub-title: Bringing The Thunder To Our Hurst Olds With 80's Style And Big Power

programme.title: Carcass
programme.desc: Our 1989 OBS Chevy C1500 truck gets a new heartbeat. We drop in the LS that Engine Power built plus add a new performance clutch, transmission, and custom exhaust.
programme.sub-title: 1989 OBS Chevy C1500 Gets a Track-Ready LS Heart Upgrade

programme.title: Music City Trucks
programme.desc: We show you all the trucks, from late models to classics, including BIGFOOT, and a drifting exhibition, that are on display to the public at the first annual Power Nationals event in Nashville.

programme.title: XOR - Xtreme Off-Road
programme.desc: Eliza and Jeremy are adding high performance brakes and working on the roll cage of their 2002 Pre-Runner!
programme.sub-title: Pre-Runner Ranger Part 3 Brake and Safety Upgrades

programme.title: Music City Trucks
programme.desc: We revisit the F150 Dream Truck and find out what bolt on upgrades actually do to your horsepower numbers, and we'll test it on the dyno.
programme.sub-title: How Much Power Can Bolt On Upgrades Add To a F-150 Sport Truck?

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: There are four basic elements that affect an engine's performance: spark, fuel, air, and lubrication. We'll show you how to improve each of them WITHOUT cracking open your powerplant.
programme.sub-title: How To Achieve Power Gains Without Taking Apart Your Engine

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Tommy and Peyton are set to get their new five-speed transmission into their Fox Body Mustang. However, due to the engine bay's shape they need to take a different approach to installing their motor-transmission duo.

programme.title: Music City Trucks
programme.desc: We buy a '89 Chevy Silverado, with aspirations of turning it into a high performing sport truck. We'll take her for a shake down run before seeing what the tired 350 can muster on the dyno. Then the transformation begins by tearing into our OBS, and stripping it to the frame, to give us a fresh canvas to start our masterpiece.

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: Our split-bumper Camaro receives a hand-crafted exhaust, designed by one of Magnaflow's own.

programme.title: Carcass
programme.desc: The Carcass crew makes modifications to the firewall of their Road Course Camaro so that the new mounting points for the engine and transmission fit. We'll also show you how to measure for custom wheels for your next project.
programme.sub-title: Camaro Racecar Body Modifications To Make Room For The Drivetrain

programme.title: Carcass
programme.desc: We work on a forgotten Chevy project, a 1996 Chevy Silverado. We head out to the junkyard to source a drivetrain, then we're back in the shop to make them roadworthy again.
programme.sub-title: Abandoned Chevy Silverado Gets A Junkyard Motor Refresh - Part 2

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: The EBC Fastback Mustang is transformed from an iconic fastback to a muscle packed stallion.
programme.sub-title: Dropping A Supercharged Coyote In The '70 RestoMod Mustang

programme.title: XOR - Xtreme Off-Road
programme.desc: We're getting the rear racing suspension installed in our 2002 Ford Ranger!

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: Turbo pioneer, Kenny Duttweiler steps in to lend a hand with our LME 427 ci LSX engine. Boosting this bullet with a high-tech turbo system produces a lot of excitement and big dyno numbers!

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: Mike and Pat stroke a vintage junkyard Ford 390 but an unexpected surprise puts a delay in their progress. Then it's full steam ahead for finding the limit for this big block stump puller
programme.sub-title: Junkyard Ford 390 FE Teardown and Rebuild

programme.title: Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live "Crushing It"
programme.desc: Here's your chance to witness the legend itself, BIGFOOT. Owner Bob Chandler takes you on the wild ride and creation of BIGFOOT, the world's first Monster Truck. As you take in the legendary tricks and stunts of BIGFOOT, you'll get to see a peek of the annual BIGFOOT open House.

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: It's a blast from the past when project Fast Lane finally sings. This 1990 Fox Body Mustang embraces the time period it came from and rides off into the wavy sunset.

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: With the paint dried, it's now time to bring our 1969 Dodge Dart one step closer to rolling! We dive deep into installing the suspension, front to back. We'll share tips that'll save your knuckles (and your sanity). We break down the process so you can tackle it solo in your own garage. Suspension isn't just about ride height, it's about control, safety, and style. Follow along as we get this Dart back on its feet.

programme.sub-title: Pre-Runner Ranger Part 3 Brake and Safety Upgrades

programme.title: Truck Tech
programme.desc: Final top end mods, rear locker & traction bars installed before our 1 ton dually hits the strip.

programme.title: Wildest Islands
programme.desc: Lying 40km off the east coast of Tanzania in Africa, the Zanzibar Archipelago has been labelled the most exotic island chain in the world. Pristine sands and azure blue sea make it a much loved holiday destination, but bizarre creatures, many of enormous size, also roam the islands. The world's largest crab scales trees in search of coconuts, and clouds of giant bats fill the skies at dusk.

programme.title: Cost of Progress
programme.desc: The natural world is in crisis. For years humanity has exploited the planet's resources, and the creatures that live here. Growth and innovation can be a marvelous thing, but at what cost to our one and only planet? When we continue to push ahead blindly, it's more often than not Mother Nature that pays the price. Now it is time for us to rally - to take heed and start to turn back the tide. It's time for us to recognize our part in this crisis and redress the balance of the cost of progress.

programme.title: Meet the Pigs
programme.desc: What first comes to mind when you think of pigs? Mud wallows and pink, curly tails? Perhaps lucky symbols and money banks, or maybe just bacon sandwiches? Whatever it is, you're probably underestimating the world's amazing collection of pigs. Today they might be one of our favourite farm animals, but if we visit their cousins in the wild we start to reveal the unique and wonderful world of the pig.

programme.title: Fighting for a Mate
programme.desc: Animals face daily battles to protect themselves and secure the resources they need to survive. Every battle is a trade-off between the risk to health and the prizes awarded to the victors. Each animal fights with a unique set of tools, from display structures and elaborate body language to claws, jaws and antlers. And few fights are as fuelled as those during breeding season; the ultimate trophy for the brave fighter is, of course, a chance to pass on the fighting genes to the next generation.

programme.title: Lion - Africa's Super Power
programme.desc: The endless plains of East Africa is a paradise for lions. The most social of all cats, lions form prides that are unlike any other animals. Together, they'll hunt, raise their young and defend their territory. With such a close family and plentiful home, the pride welcomes new babies every year. But new children introduces new dangers.

programme.title: Wildest Places: Australia
programme.desc: Wildest Places explores some of the most incredible natural habitats on earth & a diverse range of wildlife.

programme.title: Coasts - Life's a Beach
programme.desc: To us the beach is one giant playground, but for wildlife it's a place to live, to find food and to raise their young. Amongst the fish and chips, sandcastles and donkey rides it's easy to forget that beaches are vital habitats, home to a myriad of animals. Whether grey seals are duelling for a mate and raising their young, or black bears and tigers are scouring the coastline for a tasty snack, animals have been using the beach for millennia.

programme.title: Animals of Thanksgiving
programme.desc: Thanksgiving. A most treasured holiday, and not just in the USA; it continues to be celebrated across the world in many different guises. These traditions are all united by a celebration of the harvest and the generosity of the natural world. Many animals have weird and wonderful connections to the holidays. Turkeys are one of the most iconic characters, but deer, lobsters and even eagles are also part of the feast.

programme.title: Meet the Pigs
programme.desc: What first comes to mind when you think of pigs? Mud wallows and pink, curly tails? Perhaps lucky symbols and money banks, or maybe just bacon sandwiches? Whatever it is, you're probably underestimating the world's amazing collection of pigs. Today they might be one of our favourite farm animals, but if we visit their cousins in the wild we start to reveal the unique and wonderful world of the pig.

programme.title: Fight for Life
programme.desc: Nature is red in tooth and claw - animals face daily battles to protect themselves and secure the resources they need to survive. Every battle is a trade-off between energy spent, the risk to health and the prizes awarded to the victors. Each fighter has a unique set of tools and techniques available to dispatch their opponents. For predators to find food, lower links in the food chain have a fight on their hands escaping the jaws of death. Their only options are to die, run or turn and fight.

programme.title: Cost of Progress
programme.desc: The natural world is in crisis. For years humanity has exploited the planet's resources, and the creatures that live here. Growth and innovation can be a marvelous thing, but at what cost to our one and only planet? When we continue to push ahead blindly, it's more often than not Mother Nature that pays the price. Now it is time for us to rally - to take heed and start to turn back the tide. It's time for us to recognize our part in this crisis and redress the balance of the cost of progress.

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Argentina
programme.desc: Argentina's northern territory contains one of the largest reserves in the country. Iberá is a vast expanse of swamps, marshes and lagoons, with a biodiversity count to rival the Pantanal. These lands are bursting with life, home to over 4000 animal and plant species. The rainy season in Iberá finds the wetlands in bloom... but unseen perils lurk beneath the surface, and even here, life can be a struggle for survival.

programme.title: Lion - Africa's Super Power
programme.desc: The endless plains of East Africa is a paradise for lions. The most social of all cats, lions form prides that are unlike any other animals. Together, they'll hunt, raise their young and defend their territory. With such a close family and plentiful home, the pride welcomes new babies every year. But new children introduces new dangers.

programme.title: Migrations - Frequent Flyers
programme.desc: Migration is one of the most remarkable phenomena of the natural world, and perhaps the most impressive migrants of all travel on the wing.

programme.title: British Garden: Life And Death On Your Lawn
programme.desc: The British back garden is a familiar setting, but underneath the peonies and petunias is a much wilder hidden world, a miniature Serengeti, with beauty and brutality in equal measure. In this 90-minute documentary Chris Packham and a team of wildlife experts spend an entire year exploring every inch of a series of interlinked back gardens in Welwyn Garden City. They want to answer a fundamental question: how much wildlife lives beyond our back doors?

programme.title: Hawaii: Paradise in the Pacific
programme.desc: In episode two we take a look at Maui and Moloka'i. In the middle of the archipelago they form the heart of Hawaii. The second largest island of Hawai'i - Maui - is a true paradise for surfers. Archie Kalepa was one of the first big wave surfers and is still chasing the thrill today. The ukulele represents the sound of the islands like no other instrument. Eric Devine has been building the plucked string instrument for 20 years. In Kula he goes in search of the perfect wood.

programme.title: Magical Fjords
programme.desc: Fjords are one of the most dramatic landscapes on Earth, but their majesty is just the tip of the iceberg. Fjords stand witness to some of the greatest wonders of the animal kingdom. Fjords are found in a frozen land where only the toughest survive. Whether just below the surface, at the murky depths of the sea floor or on dry land, the fjords offer an incredible bounty to wildlife.

programme.title: Extinction! Going, going, gone!
programme.desc: Extinction, a daunting and confusing word. A force of nature, that sees the end of species, but also heralds the birth of others. Right now the extinction rate could be as much as 10,000 times faster than it should be. 20% of fish, a fifth of all reptiles and a quarter of mammals face extinction. If we are to do anything to stem the tide of extinction we must understand the lifestyles of those in danger.

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Islands
programme.desc: Nestled alongside Canada's south west coast, Vancouver Island is home to the richest Pacific wildlife. Sea lions and killer whales are among the marine predators enjoying the abundant seafood in the surrounding waters, while black bears, marmots and beavers enjoy the rich pickings on land. But each fall, the islands inhabitants must adapt and prepare to face the coming winter. Some will leave, among them humpback whales and turkey vultures who migrate to warmer climes.

programme.title: Wild and Alive
programme.desc: On the coast of south Africa, a group of mammoth mammals is arriving from the deep ocean. Every year humpback and southern right whales make incredible migrations from the Antarctic seas to mate and give birth along southern Africa's rich protected coast. Just arriving in time won't be enough to guarantee a mate. Humpbacks conduct awe-inspiring aerial displays and chaotic competitions for attention before showing off their grace in underwater ballets.

programme.title: Wildest Islands
programme.desc: Lying 40km off the east coast of Tanzania in Africa, the Zanzibar Archipelago has been labelled the most exotic island chain in the world. Pristine sands and azure blue sea make it a much loved holiday destination, but bizarre creatures, many of enormous size, also roam the islands. The world's largest crab scales trees in search of coconuts, and clouds of giant bats fill the skies at dusk.

programme.title: Wild and Alive
programme.desc: In the heart of the Ivory Coast a small rural village has a very special resident. The last white rhino in the country sleeps on the village outskirts and feeds on the villagers' crops. He's survived a gunshot to the shoulder and a decade of civil war, and he's something of a celebrity here. But all is not well. The rhino has killed the chief of the village, and it's time for him to go.

programme.title: Fighting for a Mate
programme.desc: Animals face daily battles to protect themselves and secure the resources they need to survive. Every battle is a trade-off between the risk to health and the prizes awarded to the victors. Each animal fights with a unique set of tools, from display structures and elaborate body language to claws, jaws and antlers. And few fights are as fuelled as those during breeding season; the ultimate trophy for the brave fighter is, of course, a chance to pass on the fighting genes to the next generation.

programme.title: January (Nature's Calendar)
programme.desc: In Europe in January, we sit around in the dark, missing the bright lights and festivities of Christmas, perhaps it would cheer us up to imagine January around the world. To the north, polar bear cubs are born and nestle against their hibernating mothers, but on the other side of the planet, kangaroos are experiencing the highest temperatures and having to trek in search of water, while in East Africa, wildebeest arrive on their breeding grounds and enjoy a baby-boom on a giant scale.

programme.title: World's Wildest City: Anchorage
programme.desc: Bred from wolves, Huskies have helped humans carve out an existence in Alaska's desolate wilderness. These dogs still maintain many physical adaptations of their wild ancestors, enabling them to withstand the fierce conditions of the Alaskan winter. And in Alaska's most extreme terrain, sled dogs are still the only form of transport. In the south, the modern city of Anchorage is still home to the start of the World's Toughest Race, a 1000 mile sled-dog race, known as the Iditarod.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Grizzly Bears, Orcas, Elephants, Wolves, Olive Baboons In many human cultures, elders play a vital role in the well-being of communities and are responsible for passing down knowledge and culture. Is it any wonder to find that the orca, the elephant, and the wolf, have been found to transmit their respective cultures to the younger generations? Young animals learn by observing their elders.

programme.title: Deserts
programme.desc: All habitats present difficulties, but the challenges of the desert are more obvious than most - scorching heat and a lack food and water make them one of the most hostile environments on the planet. But with great challenges come incredible solutions. Despite the deadly conditions, a hardy band of unique animal and plant species have adapted to meet the inhospitable desert conditions head on.

programme.title: Rhino Orphanage
programme.desc: The two oldest rhinos are set to be released back into the wild. Three rhinos cause a stir as they go missing, while the younger rhinos make steady progress toward health and happiness. A new volunteer arrives in time to see the release, but will it end in disaster?

programme.title: World of the Wild
programme.desc: The Amazon. A magnificent broad-leafed rainforest. The heart of Brazil. The Amazon basin covers an impressive 7 million square kilometres. Rainforests are often known as the lungs of our planet. The Amazon Rainforest is the largest. Its value in terms of the Oxygen that it provides, and the Carbon Dioxide that it consumes is immeasurable. It is home to splendid, exquisite plant and animal species. The most diverse and numerous array of species found anywhere in the world.

programme.title: Wildest Places: Australia
programme.desc: Wildest Places explores some of the most incredible natural habitats on earth & a diverse range of wildlife.

programme.title: Our Big Blue Backyard
programme.desc: The top of New Zealand's South Island is a landscape of two halves. To the West, one of the longest natural sandbars on the planet curves protectively around Golden Bay. To the East, mountains sink into the sea, their drowned river valleys forming the Marlborough Sounds. Turbulent currents connect them, both treacherous and full of riches.
programme.sub-title: Top of the South/ Te Tau Ihu

programme.title: Secret Life of Baby Owls
programme.desc: Owls - with their huge eyes, flat faces and distinctive hoot - they are truly iconic!creatures. But how much do we really know about these mysterious nocturnal birds? We're about to find out as we follow the fate of new born baby owls as they grow up and learn to fly.

programme.title: Wildest Survival
programme.desc: Whether by wing, fin or hoof, epic migrations are among nature's most awe-inspiring events. Animals undertake these arduous journeys, for many reasons: to find a mate, to give birth, or to move to new feeding grounds. And danger lurks at every turn. In this episode we discover the lengths they go to in order to survive.

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Argentina
programme.desc: Stretching almost 1000 miles, from the jungles of Brazil to the southernmost point of South America, Patagonia's coast is home to some of the natural world's most spectacular animals. Here, a parched desert collides with a powerful ocean, but right along this extreme and hostile coastline, animals battle the elements and each other, in a fight for survival.

programme.title: Wild and Alive
programme.desc: On the savannah of southern Africa, rains have turned the land green and lush. It's the time of plenty and for the cast of wild characters here, cashing in is priority number one. From polecat to aardwolf, some of the continent's most seldom seen creatures are out to make the most of the abundance. Some families gorge on the plentiful grasses, while for others there's no such thing as an easy meal, even at this time of year.

programme.title: Heroes of the Wild Frontiers
programme.desc: Hunting has been a long-standing cultural tradition in the North Eastern India for long. But with the shirking of the forests and endangering of the wildlife, hunting has become unsustainable. But it is not that this has stopped hunting. The architects of Pakke, a 800 sq Kms forest reserve, in the heart of the hunting villages has done a wonderful job of giving protection to the several endemic species here by keeping the forest safe from the hunters.

programme.title: March (Nature's Calendar)
programme.desc: As northern forests become carpeted by bluebells and wood anemones, and damp corners become singles bars for frogs and a toads, hailing the first hint of spring sun, South Africa needs a break from the heat, fire season is in full swing, threatening the fynbos and the extraordinary animals living in them. Ground squirrels get inventive to find shade. Gray whales migrate up the Californian coast, passing colonies of sea otters. March is a month of change

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Islands
programme.desc: The Falkland Islands' pristine coastlines and bountiful seas offer a lifeline and breeding centre for millions of penguins each year. Though while some find sanctuary on dry land, there's a daily battle to survive in the waters which surround these wild and rocky shores.

programme.title: Fight for Territory
programme.desc: Biological instinct is driven by three things: the desire to stay alive, to find food and to breed. But to do all these things, animals first need a home. Out in the wilderness a safe place to call home can be the difference between life and death. A place to secure meals, raise their families and hide from danger. Ideal spots are in short supply and well worth fighting for!

programme.title: Lions Rule
programme.desc: The Lion, Africa's ultimate predator. An essay in power and agility, famed for the cut-throat gang and the killer instinct. Lions are known as the kings of the jungle yet their homeland is an open grassland rather than rainforest. In the African plains prey-rich real estate can be hard to come by, and lions work together to ensure no one claims their territory and usurps their crown.

programme.title: Wolves - Power of the Pack
programme.desc: From arctic tundra to the great planes, the kingdom of the wolf extends across the entire northern hemisphere. They are icons of the wilderness, spectacular creatures that live and die by the sword. Though magnificent predators on their own, the feature that perhaps makes wolves so iconic is the pack. The close bonds, complex communication and sheer muscle of a team of wolves is almost unstoppable. And the pack's not just the day job, it's the cornerstone of family life for a wolf.

programme.title: Wildest Islands
programme.desc: Lying like a teardrop in the Indian Ocean, Sri Lanka is an island that defies convention. Poised just six degrees above the equator, it's less than 75,000 km sq in size. But it has enough wildlife to rival a continent, and it's all down to its complicated climate and geography.

programme.title: Heroes of the Wild Frontiers
programme.desc: Snow Leopard is the one of the most elusive big cats in the world. This episode details how the wildlife guards and the wildlife department has set up conservation and scientific plans to protect and indeed to enumerate and increase it's population. For the first time we see the radio collaring operations of the big cats and also the very rare Lynx. The episode also shows how the guards live and work in these tough terrains sometimes even by putting their lives in danger.

programme.title: Sexy Beasts
programme.desc: Driven by surging hormones, every creature on the planet, big or small, will do whatever it takes to find and secure a mate. For some this will take the fight of their lives, while others must preen, prance and party their way to success. From one night stands and group sex to lifelong love and unbreakable bonds, when it comes to finding a mate the animal kingdom has it all. The need to breed manifests itself in all sorts of wonderful antics, displays and behaviours.

programme.title: Wild Uruguay
programme.desc: Uruguay's biodiversity is surprisingly greater than one would expect. We will find out why as we embark on a journey through its ecosystems and landscapes to discover its fauna. Today we know that Uruguay is more than just the outermost edge of the Pampas, as the country holds a range of ecosystems. Within its borders, species of the Pampas come face to face with species of the Atlantic Forest, the Misiones rainforest, and the Chaco forest, giving rise to unexpected encounters.

programme.title: Wild Madagascar - Fantastic Creatures
programme.desc: Madagascar is located roughly 250 miles from Africa's Southeast Coast. It is roughly the size of France, making it the world's fourth largest island. Isolated from the African mainland for over 160 million years, more than 250,000 different species of animal can be found here; 70% of which are found nowhere else on the planet. Madagascar supports the third largest coral reef system in the world; the Toliara reef system.

programme.title: The Power Of Plants - Race to Grow and Breed
programme.desc: Just like animals, the lives of plants are dominated by the need to become strong and pass on genes to the next generation - a race to grow and breed. They must race to beat their competition to the best light spots, and to make the most of perilously short seasons. And also like in the animal kingdom, different species have developed a near unending list of strategies to ensure their legacy is passed on.

programme.title: History of Life on Earth - Journey to the Land
programme.desc: As the first landmasses emerged from prehistoric seas, animals took their first steps on dry land. The explosion of life that followed changed the world forever.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: The end is near. There have been signs and prophecies for centuries but it does feel like man's time on this planet is almost over. The question is: are you ready for Doomsday?

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: There is a secret government facility accused of creating many diseases currently plaguing our country. Have we unleashed these biological weapons on purpose and if so, is there a secret lab near you?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Certain structures on our planet have stood the test of time and continue to astonish mankind. So much so, that alien intervention in their construction thousands of years ago, has yet to be ruled out.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: In July of 2023, David Grusch, a former high ranking US Intelligence officer testified to a US government Oversight Committee that there are alien spacecraft located at secret facilities in the US.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Some places in the world, record more UAP sightings than the rest. So many so, in fact, that people flock from all over the world just for the chance to glimpse a flying saucer.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: As the Fermi Paradox states, the possibilities that there is advanced life in the universe is surprisingly high. And if the universe is so old, why haven't we had any contact with extraterrestrial life?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: There is physical evidence of alien activity that has been hidden from the public for years. It is starting to be revealed.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: It is likely that aliens exist in a universe as large as ours. How would they navigate those vast distances and potentially visit us on earth?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: There are three types of close encounters, sightings, fleeting interactions, aliens taking humans for extended periods. We meet real people who have experienced alien life up close.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Several US presidents throughout history have described encounters with UAPs. Is there already an agreement in place between our world leaders and intelligent alien life? And if so, who is keeping that information from the public and why?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: In 1998 Astronauts captured images of a satellite in Earth's orbit. Is it the same alien object that Nicola Tesla detected in 1899, an alien probe known as the Black Knight? And in 2017 scientists discovered another mysterious satellite from outside our solar system. What could explain Oumuamua's artificial trajectory?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Mars is the key focus of humanity's expansion into space right now. Millions of years ago the Red Planet had a lot in common with Earth, but it's now a desert wasteland. Do the doorways recently discovered on the planet's surface lead to an existential lesson for our species?

programme.title: UFO Diaries
programme.desc: Apparently an US base as any other, Area 51 is one of the most protected and secret military installations across the world. In 1989 a former employee called Bob Lazar declared that inside it existed alien starships and corpses investigated by engineers and scientists, creating a controversy that continues today. Is Lazar simply a liar looking for fame and fortune?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: In July of 2023, David Grusch, a former high ranking US Intelligence officer testified to a US government Oversight Committee that there are alien spacecraft located at secret facilities in the US.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Ten tales of aliens, UFOs and abductions. We'll provide a fresh look at some classic encounters and bring several new stories to light.

programme.title: Mexico Contact Point - Ebanis Mexico
programme.desc: The appearance of unidentified aerial biological entities, (ebanis), is one of the most surprising breakthroughs in the history of UFO sightings. The term Ebanis, was coined by Mexico researcher and journalist Jaime Maussan. One of these entities was recorded in video and photos by a local photographer which has puzzled scholars. What else is now known of these structures?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: As the Fermi Paradox states, the possibilities that there is advanced life in the universe is surprisingly high. And if the universe is so old, why haven't we had any contact with extraterrestrial life?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Examining the possibility that UFOs may be from Earth.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: In 1947, a series of UFO sightings triggers an unprecedented analysis that propels the UFO phenomenon on to the world stage. We investigate how the U.S. Air Force comes to the stunning conclusion that UFOs may not be from Earth.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: UFO sightings happen almost every day. But in the court of public opinion the most credible witnesses come from law enforcement. Join us as we investigate the most important police sightings of UFOs.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Between 1981 and 2011, NASA's Space Shuttles flew 135 missions. The Space Shuttle cameras, manned and unmanned, have recorded astounding footage of UFOs that many experts find almost impossible to explain.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Scientists have never been closer to proving that life once lived on Mars. But is it still there? And if so, how has it evolved? Join us as we investigate the red planet and the possibility that alien life may live within our own galaxy.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Scientists and Ufologists are scouring the vast regions of space for signs of extraterrestrial life. But if it takes millions of years for light from distant stars to reach Earth, how long could it take for aliens to answer our call?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Some scientists believe the survival of mankind hinges upon the revolutionary science of Artificial Intelligence. Biological life may just be an evolutionary stepping-stone in a universe dominated by Artificial Alien Intelligence.

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: For decades, Kent's Blue Bell Hill has been the site of mysterious phenomena. Rumored ghost sightings have haunted the pastoral site. Explore the haunting legacy of Blue Bell Hill in this episode.
programme.sub-title: The Mystery of Blue Bell Hill

programme.title: The Past Hunters: Enter the Paranormal
programme.desc: The former home of Queen Victoria is now home to many spirits who have been seen by guests and staff. Witness the first ever formal documentation of the paranormal activities in the Bulkeley Hotel.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension Flying Solo
programme.desc: Sean heads to Macclesfield, Cheshire to investigate a building said to be haunted by 14 ghosts and also the lost soul of a witch. With so many spirits and one of the oldest public houses in the UK, will any of the ghosts join him tonight?

programme.title: The Past Hunters: Enter the Paranormal
programme.desc: The former home of Queen Victoria is now home to many spirits who have been seen by guests and staff. Witness the first ever formal documentation of the paranormal activities in the Bulkeley Hotel.

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: Bonnybridge, a village in Scotland, has long been shrouded in paranormal mystery. Are the flying objects hovering above its skies connected to alien life? Explore the mystery in this episode.

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: Malahide, a village in Ireland, has been attached to rumors of reincarnation and near-death experiences. Explore the mystery of Malahide in this episode.
programme.sub-title: Malahide, the Edge of Life and Death

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: Since its origin in 1196, Micklegate Bar, a massive entrance to the city of York, has been host to royal powers, Lords, and also some other guests, those from a world beyond ours.

programme.title: Nazi Creatures
programme.desc: Hitler, Goring, Himmler: the three architects of the Final Solution. They, like many other high ranking Nazis, shared a fascination with the animal world. In the last days of the Nazi regime, Hitler risked his life every day, leaving the safety of the bunker to walk his beloved dog, Blondi. But the Nazis' interest went beyond love of their pets or the animal welfare laws they introduced.

programme.title: Mysteries of Stonehenge
programme.desc: On the grassy chalk-land of the Salisbury plain, two hours southwest of London, there looms a remarkable stone monument. It certainly seems that Stonehenge is a silent remnant of another age...a reminder of man's primordial beginnings. There are countless legends about its origin and purpose. Who built it? How and when was it built? And most intriguing of all, what is it?

programme.title: The Magic of Houdini: The Illusions and Stunts of Harry Houdini
programme.desc: Having been fascinated with magic since he was a boy, Alan Davies explores the life of illusionist and stunt performer, Harry Houdini, who became one of the most successful entertainers in the world. Alan holds his breath underwater, lies on a bed of nails, gets strung upside down in a straitjacket and takes an exclusive look at David Copperfield's collection of Houdini artefacts in Vegas.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension
programme.desc: Bex and Sean head to Sefton and investigate a police station connected to the murderous Jack The Ripper. Was James Maybrick really the Ripper? Did his wife poison him? Is he haunting this old police station? These are the questions Ghost Dimension investigate tonight.

programme.title: The Conspiracy Show with Richard Syrett
programme.desc: Richard meets with some prominent JFK assassination researchers who assert that the November 1963 murder of President John F. Kennedy was nothing less than a coup d' tat. They believe it was orchestrated by a powerful cabal inside the military industrial complex.

programme.title: The Conspiracy Show with Richard Syrett
programme.desc: Richard investigates a UFO sighting over Chicago's O'Hare airport that was witnessed by dozens of people, including an airline captain, his crew and several airport officials.

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: Since the beginning of time man has expressed his religious beliefs through rock art, it gives the feeling that he has worshipped some mysterious gods, that generally came from the stars. Over the millennia, these gods have changed in shape and name, but the way they have been disguised in our beliefs remains the same, in many cases to the misfortune of the witnesses.

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: From Mafasca, in the plains of Fuerteventura, to Pardal, in the mountains of Albacete, passing through the light of Cayón in Cantabria, we are talking about intelligent luminosities. These are seen at night and have even followed witnesses. They are the most commonly seen lights, undoubtedly a phenomenon that is part of another of the strangest aspects of the UFO theme: The foo- fighters.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: New developments in science and research have invented equipment that may have much more sinister capabilities than we are being led to believe. Are governments around the world using weather control to incite the next World War and possibly destroy the planet?

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: The past few decades have been filled with stunning technological advancement. But is all this 'progress' good for humanity? Animal cloning has been a reality for decades but the disturbing experiments going on behind close doors will shock you. Human cloning may be much closer than you think.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Is this half man, half ape simply a figment of our collective imagination or does he really exist? As the evidence begins to pile up maybe we should be asking: who has been keeping this from us?

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: The Great Deceiver. Seducer of the masses. The Bringer of Armageddon. Every culture and religion on the planet believes that an evil one will usher in the end of days. But who is this Anti-Christ? And how can we hope to stop him?

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Scientists believe that Stargates are doorways to wormholes in time. As it turns out, the government may have already known that. We'll reveal the secret location of stargates around the world and tell you who is trying to open them and why.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files counts down the top 10 conspiracies of all time: (10) the moon landing hoax, (9) MK Ultra mind control experiments, (8) the secret Area 51 air force base, (7) the H.A.A.R.P. antenna installation, (6) Chemtrails in the atmosphere, (5) the New World Order, (4) the Jesus was married conspiracy, (3) the Roswell incident, (2) Hitler's Death, and (1) the JFK assassination.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files looks at how the Soviet Union and the United States sponsored experiments in remote viewing during the Cold War. It also looks at how the CIA spent $20 million dollars investigating remote viewing as a part of Project Stargate. It also discusses how remote viewers were used to look for the Mars Observer and a possible Mars Base.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files looks at how some world leaders throughout history have used impostors and doubles. It considers theories whether Osama bin Laden had a double, Elizabeth I died in her youth and was replaced by a boy, George Washington was replaced by the head of the Illuminati Adam Weishaupt, and that Hitler faked his suicide and fled to Argentina.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: According to physics, time travel is possible. So could it be that UAPs aren't coming from somewhere else, but from some when else. Could these UAPs be us, from the future?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Certain structures on our planet have stood the test of time and continue to astonish mankind. So much so, that alien intervention in their construction thousands of years ago, has yet to be ruled out.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Some places in the world, record more UAP sightings than the rest. So many so, in fact, that people flock from all over the world just for the chance to glimpse a flying saucer.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: UAPs have only recently been witnessed entering the ocean at very high speeds. And since our oceans can be as much as six miles deep, is it possible that some of these UAPs were simply trying to get home?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: As the Fermi Paradox states, the possibilities that there is advanced life in the universe is surprisingly high. And if the universe is so old, why haven't we had any contact with extraterrestrial life?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: It is likely that aliens exist in a universe as large as ours. How would they navigate those vast distances and potentially visit us on earth?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: There are three types of close encounters, sightings, fleeting interactions, aliens taking humans for extended periods. We meet real people who have experienced alien life up close.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: From military radar to Navy aircraft, sightings of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena have become more frequent of late and been measured on ever more sophisticated technology. It has lead to unprecedented acceptance of alien contact across the globe, including by the US government. What could these visitors be after? Is it the potential energy stored in the Earth's oceans?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Several US presidents throughout history have described encounters with UAPs. Is there already an agreement in place between our world leaders and intelligent alien life? And if so, who is keeping that information from the public and why?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Everyday, UFOs are spotted in skies all over the world. But of all the planets in the known galaxy, why have they come to Earth? Are aliens here to seize Earth's riches? And how far does their mission go?

programme.title: UFO Casebook
programme.desc: Of all the various kinds of UFO related phenomenon that has materialized, the so called light spheres certainly hold a particularly important place. These objects have recently gained great popularity thanks in part to the studies conducted by Dr. Eltjo Haselhoff, who believes that these light spheres could be the cause behind crop circles. The lights began to appear many years ago...but why?

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: These attacks are the most terrifying part of the phenomenon, and therefore, the most real. Attacks in the middle of the morning, like what happened with Nicolás Sánchez Martín, in Cáceres, or Joan Turu and José Félix Rodríguez, better known as the suicide bombers of Tarrasa, can lead to the death of the witnesses. What is behind these aggressive apparitions?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: In 1998 Astronauts captured images of a satellite in Earth's orbit. Is it the same alien object that Nicola Tesla detected in 1899, an alien probe known as the Black Knight? And in 2017 scientists discovered another mysterious satellite from outside our solar system. What could explain Oumuamua's artificial trajectory?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Examining the possibility that UFOs may be from Earth.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: For decades, scientists have been searching for proof that extraterrestrials exist. But just where does alien life exist? And what does it look like? Join us as we investigate just how close we are to First Contact.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: A mysterious book, 'The Blue Planet Project' has surfaced, outlining decades of cooperation between the U.S. military and alien forces on earth as well as a massive government cover-up to hide these visitors from the world.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Aliens have been trying to make contact with mankind for millennia. Now for the first time, one of those messages has been decoded and we will share that message with the world.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Could one of the most sacred place on Earth also house secret knowledge of extraterrestrial life? The path to disclosure just might lie on holy ground: at the Vatican.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Tampered space photos, missing NASA recordings and a race to the moon all point to one very likely possibility: alien life exists, and our universe is anything but our own.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Since the dawn of man, unexplained illnesses have attacked the human population with a vengeance. Are these diseases the result of a secret alien agenda to take over Planet Earth? Tonight, we unseal the truth behind these Alien Plagues.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Ten tales of aliens, UFOs and abductions. We'll provide a fresh look at some classic encounters and bring several new stories to light.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension Lockdown
programme.desc: Bex and Sean investigate a haunted cottage hidden deep in the heart of Cheshire. Believed to be haunted by a family of ghostly spirits, many urban explorers have encountered paranormal activity inside of the building.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension
programme.desc: Join Bex, Sean and the team as they investigate The Wellington Hotel for Halloween. Based in Halewood, this public inn has more haunting inside of its walls than the spirits behind the bar.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension Flying Solo
programme.desc: Sean heads to Stockport to investigate a haunted mill, which has a lift with a mind all of its own. Will any of the ghosts haunting the mill join him on the investigation tonight or will it all go pear shaped?
programme.sub-title: Will it All Go Pear Shaped at Pear Mill? - Part 1

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: Since its origin in 1196, Micklegate Bar, a massive entrance to the city of York, has been host to royal powers, Lords, and also some other guests, those from a world beyond ours.

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: For decades, Kent's Blue Bell Hill has been the site of mysterious phenomena. Rumored ghost sightings have haunted the pastoral site. Explore the haunting legacy of Blue Bell Hill in this episode.
programme.sub-title: The Mystery of Blue Bell Hill

programme.title: The SS and The Occult
programme.desc: This powerful film revisits the sites most closely associated with Heinrich Himmler and traces the development of his warped ideology. Heinrich Himmler was the creator of the infamous Gestapo, the Waffen SS and the concentration camp network. He was inspired by mystic visions, runes, horoscopes and a longing for a heroic German past. The occult roots of the Third Reich are discussed.

programme.title: The Real Merlin
programme.desc: His name conjures up images of a golden age of magic, mystery and chivalry. Of Camelot and the search for the Holy Grail, King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table. But is there any truth behind the myth of Merlin, a man beyond the legend? The Real Merlin finds a sixth-century druid, shaman and right-hand man to the last pagan king, a prophet who predicted his own strange three-fold death.

programme.title: On the Yeti Trail
programme.desc: Does the Yeti really exist? Our film sets out to meet the teams involved in this strange race across the world, and features laboratories, hair analysis, footprints and DNA as well as the search for samples in Indonesia and in Canadian nature reserves. A fascinating and thorough film, featuring, amongst others, French Collège de France paleoanthropologist Pascal Picq.

programme.title: Vampire Skeletons
programme.desc: In summer 2007, at a site in Ireland, archaeologists were uncovering layers of graves. They were astonished to find two skeletons with large stones lodged in their jaws. The archaeologists believe that the skeletons were treated as if they were 'revenants' - individuals who might return from the dead to prey on the living.

programme.title: The Conspiracy Show with Richard Syrett
programme.desc: Richard travels to Kent in the south of England to investigate reports of werewolf sightings. He meets with an acclaimed paranormal investigator in New York's Central Park who separates fact from fiction regarding the legend of the werewolf, and a journalist describes eye-witness accounts of a bi-pedal, wolf-like creature said to be haunting a lonely stretch of road in Wisconsin.

programme.title: The Conspiracy Show with Richard Syrett
programme.desc: Richard speaks with several independent researchers about their allegations that a powerful, secretive cabal of international bankers is attempting to rule the course of history and imprison humanity through their monopoly of the creation and control of the planet's money supply.

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: What can lead a military man to draw his service weapon in his own base, and completely unload the magazine of his rifle? In the cases that we are going to analyze, these military men claim to have witnessed the appearance of strange humanoid beings.

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: Explore mysterious sightings spanning millennia, from ancient rock art to recent encounters. Witness strange lights over Barranco de Badajoz and a peculiar being at 'El Condesito' farm in Huelva. Encounter enigmatic humanoids on Conil beaches. Hear from witnesses to unravel the uncanny connection between past depictions and present sightings.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files examines whether the United States has been involved in a secret conflict with alien forces for the past fifty years. It looks at the Battle of Los Angeles and the Roswell Incident. It also discusses the theory that President Eisenhower made a treaty with alien race.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files examines whether time travel is real and, if it is, whether it is under the control of a mysterious elite. It examines the mysterious South Fork Bridge photo which purports to show a man out of time. It also looks at theories that claim that the Nazis developed a time travel device during World War II.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files considers the theory that Adolph Hitler survived the end of the World War II. It looks at Operation Paperclip which allowed many Nazi scientists to come to the United States and considers Hitler possible escape to Argentina with assistance from the FBI. It also discusses continued Nazi influence in history.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files counts down the top ten secret societies: (10) The Hellfire Club, (9) The Majestic Twelve, (8) The Knights of the Golden Circle, (7) Opus Dei, (6) The Bohemian Club, (5) Skull and Bones, (4) The Bilderberg Group, (3) The Knights Templar, (2) The Freemasons, and (1) The Illuminati.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files looks at some of the secret government warehouses of the United States. It looks at Fort Knox gold depository and asks whether the gold there has been removed. It also examines Hangar 18 at Wright Patterson Air Force base in Ohio and whether it contains crashed alien craft or the Nazi Die Glocke.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files examines a conspiracy that may be seeking to eradicate 90% of the world's population. It looks at the Georgia Guidestones built by an unknown architect which call for humanity to reduce its population to below 500 million.

programme.title: The Miracle Of The Cards
programme.desc: There's no such thing as miracles. That's what a skeptical reporter (Kirk Cameron) thought until he met Craig Shergold (Thomas Sangster). Craig is an eight-year-old boy with a brain tumor and less than a year to live. Looking for hope, his mother (Catherine Oxenberg) pushes to break the Guinness World Record for receiving the most get-well cards. They receive an incredible 1.3 million cards and shatter the old record. However Craig continues to get worse.

programme.title: Hank's Christmas Wish
programme.desc: "Hank's Christmas Wish" tells the heartwarming tale of a retired elf seeking a life of seclusion. However, his plans are interrupted when a group of unrelentingly cheerful townsfolk, brimming with the holiday spirit, come into his life. Through their unwavering kindness and infectious joy, they help him rediscover the true meaning of Christmas. Packed with yuletide laughter, chestnut-roasting moments, and Jack Frost-nipping faith, this cutesy film captures the essence of the holiday season.

programme.title: By God's Grace
programme.desc: In the tradition of a classic "A Christmas Carol", this film offers many lessons on the importance of giving and the cause and effect our choices have on others.

programme.title: My Son, My Savior
programme.desc: A powerful portrayal of the life of Jesus as seen through the eyes of his mother, Mary. The film imagines Mary's childhood, growing up, celebrating the annual feasts and hearing the prophecies about a coming Messiah who would redeem Israel.

programme.title: Finding Christmas
programme.desc: Mikey Finnegan, a 17-year-old from Philly, dreams of becoming a pro gamer. After a Christmas Eve attack leaves him in a coma, he travels back to Bethlehem. Guided by a Guardian Angel, he must find baby Jesus to return home.

programme.desc: Noah Davis is a Pastor in an affluent community. With Christmas approaching, he packs up and together with his two daughters, moves into Salvation Street Mission. Now the family must struggle with the challenges they face in the crime ridden community.

Now, the more Jake learns of the power within the box and its purpose, the more obstacles he must overcome to get the box to a stranger before it's too late.

programme.title: The Elf on the Shelf: Sweet Showdown
programme.desc: At the Scout Elves' Enchanted Cottage, Duff Goldman asks the teams to create an edible shelf for their own Scout Elf; the bottom teams must impress judges Kardea Brown and Ashley Holt with their memory-filled snow globe showpieces.

programme.title: The Elf on the Shelf: Sweet Showdown

programme.title: The Elf on the Shelf: Sweet Showdown
programme.desc: The Scout Elves want to play the "12 Days of Christmas" at their concert, but they mix up the lyrics; Duff Goldman tasks the teams with delivering a twisted-up "12 Days of Elfmas" showpiece.

programme.title: The Elf on the Shelf: Sweet Showdown
programme.desc: The scout elves have some trouble tuning up Santa's sleigh, so Duff Goldman asks the teams to create a sleigh design that will wow Mr. Claus; two teams build inventive snow forts for a snowball fight between judges Kardea Brown and Ashley Holt.

programme.title: The Elf on the Shelf: Sweet Showdown
programme.desc: The scout elves fly over their favorite places as they return to the North Pole, so Duff Goldman challenges the finalists to elf-ify a famous landmark; Kardea Brown and Ashley Holt award their Ambassadors of Confectionery Concoctions with $25,000.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Autumn-inspired food, including chai chocolate truffles, white velvet soup, spicy cocktail puffs and jam cocktails.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Holiday dishes with a modern spin, including pumpkin alfredo lasagna rolls, crispy truffled turkey and caramelized apple semifreddo cake.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: A cocktail-style Thanksgiving celebration with appetizer-sized versions of beloved holiday dishes, like stuffing arancini, turkey Waldorf bites, charred brussels sprout crostini and a mulled cosmo cocktail.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Roasted fennel with parmesan; creamy lobster pasta; chocolate almond cheesecake; citrus berry vermouth spritz.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Indulgent desserts and sparkling cocktails, including orange mousse with ginger snap crumble, peppermint patty sandwich cookies, hazelnut torte with chocolate espresso frosting and lemon hazelnut spritz cocktails.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada treats her daughter Jade and friends to a party, where each guest makes their own gingerbread house; kid-friendly treats like s'mores popcorn, pizza grilled cheese, veggie forest with parmesan ranch dip and frozen hot chocolate affogatos.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada hosts a Christmas dinner for family and friends; on the menu, tortellini in parmesan brodo, risotto with clams, braised lamb shanks with escarole and radicchio and a chocolate candy cane tower.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada hosts a Halloween open house for neighborhood trick-or-treaters and their parents; Giada creates spooky menu for her guests which includes Coconut Bones, Spooky Chicken Finger Sammies, Witches' Brooms and Here's Looking at Boo Treats.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis hosts a fancy, vintage-inspired cocktail party and serves throwback recipes with a modern twist like bacon onion dip, a spiked gelatin mold and a Korean shrimp cocktail.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis asks her Thanksgiving guests to each bring something to add to a large antipasti platter; spicy turkey breast cacciatorel; smokey candied carrots and walnut gremolata; simple wilted greens; chocolate chunk hazelnut pie.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: The morning after Thanksgiving, Giada De Laurentiis feeds her guests with a brunch made from Thanksgiving leftovers; crispy turkey bites; cheesy root vegetable bake; sweet potato puffs; rye-spiked chai lattes.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis throws a pre-Christmas party for the kids; holiday sing-along; cheesy chicken flautas; veggie voodle salad; chocolate-covered chips; apple pie soda a la mode.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis' family members exchange Secret Santa gifts; stuffed tricolore pork loin; roasted acorn squash agrodolce; chopped romaine and radicchio salad; black and white brownie ice cream cake.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: One of Trisha Yearwood's favorite spots in Nashville is The Loveless Cafe; she spends the day putting a spin on her favorite dishes from the restaurant with recipes like cheesy angel biscuits and cornbread crusted fried pork chops.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada has a step-by-step approach for planning and executing Thanksgiving; lemon and pea alfredo; sweet and savory kale salad; prosciutto wrapped turkey; for dessert, mascarpone cannoli cheesecake.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: It's the day after Thanksgiving, and that usually means three things: college football, Christmas shopping and Thanksgiving leftovers; Giada marks the official start of the Christmas season with wrapping gifts and delicious food.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: A Christmas cocktail party and silly Santa gift exchange; holiday appetizers and favorite karaoke tunes; spinach artichoke panini bites; warm citrus marinated olives; chocolate coconut cake and burnt citrus cocktails.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis and her daughter Jade host a Christmas party for Jade and her friends; Giada prepares a batch of holiday cutout sugar cookies that the kids can decorate using a variety of fun toppings and frosting.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: In Italy, the night before Christmas is celebrated with the Feast of the Seven Fishes, and Giada De Laurentiis hosts a family Christmas Eve dinner that honors this tradition.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis kicks off the season with a buffet brunch that features the flavors of autumn; bacon cranberry scones with citrus basil butter; sweet potato; kale Spanish frittata; smoked salmon waffles with waffle bar; apple raspberry sangrias.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: A look back at some great game day and tailgating recipes; jalapeno-stuffed curly dogs, buffalo pierogies, baked chicken tenders with cheese cracker breading and no-bake rocky road bars.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis hosts an open house and makes a variety of Italian-themed appetizers; goat cheese-stuffed baby peppers; crispy chicken meatballs; shrimp fra diavolo bites; chocolate Christmas tree brownies; a whiskey spritz cocktail.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada hosts a party where guests are asked to come dressed as their favorite holiday song; guests enjoy Giada's festive menu that includes a mozzarella bar, chicken piccata skewers, slow-roasted mustard salmon and a Sparkling Cosmo Punch.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada hosts a holiday party for kids and transforms the house into a winter wonderland; guests get to make their own snow globes and enjoy a menu of creamy tomato soup, triple chocolate hot cocoa, crispy chicken sandwiches and Italian flag cookies.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada hosts family Christmas dinner and pulls out all the stops with a fun gift exchange and an elegant menu; she makes a simple standing rib roast, Blistered Baby Pepper Salad, cavatelli with Gorgonzola and tomatoes and a panettone trifle.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada hosts a harvest-themed festival for her neighbors; the feast includes roasted squash and gorgonzola pizza, made with Giada's own pizza dough, complemented with Italian carrot salad and spiced apple cake.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada asks each family member to invite a friend and provides a personalized welcome message, the guests enjoy a menu of braised turkey braciole, bacon stuffing with radicchio and chestnuts, Brussels sprouts agrodolce and parmesan Apple Pie.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis and her daughter, Jade, host a holiday party for friends; Jade helps prepare the menu, prep for the party and plan the activity of making homemade Christmas gifts for a teacher; the menu is a gourmet twist on kid favorites.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada De Laurentiis invites her cousins to bring an appetizer over for a Christmas party, and surprise guest Aunt Raffy judges which is the best; after the highly competitive game, Giada and her guests dine on a festive buffet-style meal.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada is on a mission to recreate a family holiday recipe called miracle rice with her Aunt Raffy; the dish reflects generations of stories and memories; they also create a simple sorbet before ending the night with a grab-bag gift exchange.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada hosts a formal brunch for her family on Christmas day, with a California twist; her menu includes beef tenderloin with scallion salsa verde, a crab and artichoke frittata, olive biscuits and a decadent chocolate panettone sformato for dessert.

programme.title: Giada's Holiday Handbook
programme.desc: Giada helps her girlfriends jump-start the new year with a fun gathering that focuses on wellness and self-care; she serves a buffet menu of her healthy wedge salad, broiled salmon with fennel salad, and herb de provence roasted potatoes.

programme.desc: Eddie Jackson mistakenly grabs his box of Halloween cookie cutters from the attic; five cookie makers must hack the Halloween cutters into classic Christmas cookies.

programme.desc: For the decorating challenge, five of the cleverest cookie makers design two different cookies: one showcasing Santa's new outfit and another featuring his new ride; Vivian Chan, Ree Drummond and Gesine Prado judge.

programme.desc: Five creative cookie makers are dreaming of a white Christmas as Eddie Jackson challenges them to decorate cookies using only detail, texture and relief.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

programme.desc: New York, New York: Join Anthony Bourdain on his quest to characterize the perfect bar. With him, discover the importance of a "maniacal bartender", the proper chemical makeup of drinks, the joys of seedy dive-bars, and the need for late night snacks.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.desc: Arcachon, France Here, Bourdain first learned to love food as a child. Returning for a trip down memory lane, Tony enjoys childhood staples, including steak frites, gaufres (waffles), soupe de pecheur (fishermans soup) and fresh oysters.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

In search of the outlaws of food, Tony explores a pasteurization-free cheese factory, and an old-world cured jamon workshop. Alas, no trip to Australia is complete without an authentic "barbie", so Bourdain settles down with new found friends for an afternoon meal of surf n' turf.
programme.sub-title: Down Under: The Wild West of Cooking

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

programme.sub-title: San Sebastian: A Food Lover's Town

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

programme.sub-title: Eating on the Edge of Nowhere

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

From spicy soups and noodles in the busy city, to the hospitality and delicate salads of the countryside, Tony learns to appreciate all things Thai.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

programme.sub-title: Puebla, Where the Good Cooks Are From

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

programme.sub-title: So Much Vodka, So Little Time

programme.sub-title: Singapore: New York in Twenty Years

Mr. Bourdain, under the tutelage of an exemplary Carioca, gives the lifestyle a try, enjoying a savage tan, Brazilian barbecue, and one too many Caipirinhas!

programme.desc: In mid-August 1944, the Allies launched 'Operation Anvil' to increase pressure on German troops after the Normandy landings. The 517th Airborne was tasked with preventing enemy tanks from reaching the beachhead. This episode recounts the story of three American sergeants and a British major who jumped into enemy territory, successfully completed their mission, and survived to tell the tale.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Marines in Combat
programme.desc: The Marines move on to Okinawa, with periods of rest and recuperation between fighting.

programme.desc: The Allied landings on D Day and the subsequent battles for control of Normandy.
